summary: Created src/setup/runner.ts with runSetup(components, args): handles --all (select all), --components=a,b / --components a,b (select subset), non-TTY guard (prints error and returns 1), interactive TTY path (delegates to runCheckboxMenu), summary table with success/failure counts, and exit code 1 on any failure.
Created src/setup/index.ts barrel exporting runSetup and runCheckboxMenu.
Created tests/setup/runner.test.ts with 17 tests covering all acceptance criteria. All 161 tests pass, no regressions.

comments.note: runner.ts resolveSelectedIds() handles both --components=a,b and --components a,b forms for ergonomic CLI usage; the two-token form also guards against a missing or flag-like next argument and returns a descriptive error.
No code smells observed in the touched files. checkbox-menu.ts and colors.ts are clean and consistent with the project style.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified — manual code review + automated test suite (180 tests, 0 failures).
Build check: TypeScript typecheck clean (tsc --noEmit, no errors).
Regression check: full suite passed with no regressions. Developer reported 161 tests; suite now stands at 180 (reflects cumulative additions from WP-003 and WP-004).
AC1 (--all): resolveSelectedIds() maps all component IDs when FLAG_ALL is present. Two tests cover success and failure paths.
AC2 (--components a,b): both equals form (--components=a,b) and two-token form (--components a,b) tested and verified. Error path (missing value) also covered.
AC3 (Non-TTY without flags): guards isTTY before entering interactive path; prints descriptive error to stderr and returns 1. Test uses Object.defineProperty to simulate non-TTY.
AC4 (Summary table): printSummary() writes component labels, ✔/✘ symbols, and 'N succeeded / N failed' counts. Test asserts all four content pieces.
AC5 (Exit code 1 on failure): results.every() used cleanly; three independent tests confirm exit code semantics.
AC6 (Barrel export): src/setup/index.ts re-exports runSetup and runCheckboxMenu. Two barrel tests verify dynamic import.

metrics.test_coverage: 17 new tests cover all 6 ACs; full suite green

comments.note: runner.ts silently drops unrecognised component IDs when a --components subset is specified — only matched IDs run. If ALL IDs are unrecognised it returns exit 1 with an error, but a partial mismatch is not flagged. Consider adding a warning line per unknown ID for better developer ergonomics. Not a blocking issue.

component.run(args) is called without a try/catch. A thrown exception would propagate out of runSetup unhandled, skipping the summary table. No AC requires exception handling here, but a future hardening pass could wrap the call.
No test for --components= (empty equals form). The code correctly returns an error ('No component IDs supplied'), but coverage would be improved with a dedicated case.

comments.note: runner.ts resolveSelectedIds() two-token branch: replaced `return { ids: ids.length > 0 ? ids : null, error: ids.length > 0 ? null : '…' }` with an early-return guard followed by `return { ids, error: null }`. Matches the early-return style used in the equals-form branch immediately above it. Purely cosmetic — program behaviour and all tests unchanged.

runner.ts: when --components specifies IDs that partially overlap the registered component list, unrecognised IDs are silently dropped (the all-unknown case correctly returns exit 1). A per-unknown-ID warning line would improve CLI ergonomics in future. Not blocking.

runner.ts: component.run(args) is called without a try/catch. A thrown exception propagates out of runSetup unhandled, bypassing the summary table. Out of scope for this WP; worth a dedicated hardening pass later.

[documentation-forward] resolveSelectedIds() is a non-trivial internal function with three distinct parsing paths. A brief JSDoc comment (e.g. 'Parse --all / --components flag from argv; returns resolved IDs or an error string') would help future contributors navigate runner.ts without reading the full implementation.
